summary: Ensho Kobayashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held posts at Hanazono University as a professor (attested 1988) and later as professor emeritus (attested 2026).

Ensho Nasu works in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Ryukoku University under doctoral supervisor Esho Mikogami (attested 1996) and served as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University (attested 2007).

Enshu Kurumiya specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Yukio Sakamoto, Ensho Kanakura, Yosho Nomura, and Jan Willem de Jong, completing his PhD at the Australian National University in 1974, and was a professor at Rissho University (attested 1981-1985).

Entai Tomomatsu (1895-1973) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Keio University around 1920-1923. He held a post at Taisho University and founded the Publishing Association of Abhidharmakosa-vyakhya.

Erberto Lo Bue (1946-2022) specialized in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London (~1976-1981) and held appointments at the University of Milan (attested 1996) and the University of Bologna (~1997-2011).

Eric David Mortensen works in Tibetology and religious studies. He completed a PhD at Harvard University (attested 2003) under Leonard van der Kuijp, Michael Witzel, and Kimberley C. Patton, also studying under Chongren He, Xiaoxun He, Zhiben He, Xi Aniu, and Xuewen He.

Eric George Hart (1878-1946) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Wellington College and Victoria College, Jersey, and served as Professor of Arabic, Persian and Hindustani and Reader of Indian History at Trinity College Dublin (1926-1938).
Eric Haruki Swanson works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held a post at Loyola Marymount University and was a Senior Visiting Scholar at Stanford University (attested 2026).
Eric Huntington is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Gary A. Tubb.

Eric J. Sharpe (1933-2000) was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. Educated at Manchester and Uppsala under Bengt Sundkler, he held posts at Manchester, Lancaster, Uppsala (Professor, 1978-1981), and the University of Sydney (Chair of Religious Studies, 1977-1996).

Eric M. Greene specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at UC Berkeley under Robert H. Sharf and others, later serving as an assistant professor at San Francisco State University (2023) and at Yale University (attested 2017; associate professor attested 2026).

Eric P. Hamp (1920-2019) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. Educated at Amherst College and Harvard University under Joshua Whatmough, he held posts at the University of Michigan and the University of Chicago (~1950-1991).

Eric Stephen Goodell specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned an MA from the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and an MA from the University of Virginia (attested 2012), where he studied under Paul Groner.

Eric Thomas Stokes (1924-1981) was a historian who completed his PhD at Cambridge under Thomas George Percival Spear. He held posts at the University of Malaya, Bristol, Zimbabwe, and served as Smuts Professor at Cambridge from 1970 to 1981.
Eric Villalobos is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He has been affiliated with the Graduate Division of Religion and studied as a doctoral student at Emory University (attested 2026).

Erica Baffelli works in Japanology and religious studies. Having studied under Massimo Raveri, she held a post at the University of Otago (attested 2015) and has served as Professor in Japanese Studies at the University of Manchester (attested 2016, 2026).
Erica Biagetti is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and computational approaches. She completed her PhD at the University of Pavia by 2021 and also held a post there.

Erich Arno Lehmann (1901-1984) worked in Indology and religious studies. He completed a Dr.Theol. at Leipzig and held posts at Leipzig (~1948-1950), Jena (~1950-1967), and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1950-1966) as Dean of the Theological Faculty.

Erich Berneker (1874-1937) was a linguist who earned his PhD at Leipzig under August Leskien. He held professorships at the German University in Prague (1902-1909), the University of Breslau (1909-1911), and the University of Munich (1911).

Erich Frauwallner (1898-1974) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Vienna under Bernhard Geiger and served as a professor and director there across 1928-1964, also editing Wiener Zeitschrift für die Kunde Süd- und Ostasiens.
